**What you’re asking for** You’d like a page where users can: 1. **Sign‑in with email (magic link or code).** 2. **Upload a photo of their pet (only image files, size‑limit, stored in a private bucket).** 3. **See a feed of other pets’ photos and click “Like” on them (they can only like each person’s own photos once).** No payments or personal data beyond the photo link, so we’re an **Amber** app. --- ### Safety parts that will be built in | Feature | Safety part | |---|---| | 📸 **Photo uploads** | • Only the uploader can add, change or delete their own files.
• Only `.jpg/.png` files under 5 MB will be accepted.
• Files go into a private Supabase bucket.
• If you see a photo that shouldn’t be public, you can flag it for review. | | 👍 **Likes** | • Users can only like each photo once.
• Liking a photo does not expose the uploader’s email or any other private data.
• A simple anti‑spam rule (max 20 likes per day per user). | --- ### Starter questions (just 3) 1. **Who will use the app?** - a) Just friends/family (small group) - b) Open to the public (anyone with an email) 2. **What do you want the feed to look like first?** - e.g. “Show 12 newest photos, with the owner’s nickname and date” 3. **Do you want a way for users to see only their own photos (e.g., a “My‑Pets” page)?** Feel free to answer all or just the ones you think matter; we’ll fill in the rest. --- ### One‑screen plan (draft) ``` What we are building: A pet‑photo sharing page. Who uses it: Public / small group (answer Q1) Risk level: Amber (sign‑in, uploads, likes) Day‑one features: 1. Sign‑in with email via magic link. 2. Upload photo → stored in private bucket (max 5 MB, .jpg/.png). 3. Public feed showing newest photos, with owner nickname, date, and a Like button. 4. "My Pets" page (optional, answers Q3). Information it stores: photos, upload timestamps, owner ID, like counts (private). Logins: email‑only magic link (Supabase Auth). Money: none. Built with: React (Next.js) + Supabase (Auth, Storage, Postgres). Steps: 1. Add Supabase credentials, set up auth, bucket, and tables. 2. Build upload form with client‑side validation. 3. Create post‑upload GraphQL/REST mutation to record photo metadata. 4. Show feed with privacy‑safe queries, add like mutation with per‑user limit. 5. Apply RLS policies on tables and storage. Safety: keys secret (in .env), data locked to owner, two‑strike rule on failures, save points before each step. ``` Does this look right? Reply “yes” or tell me what to change.
